about: The budgets of PrompTugal.news: per agent per day, per pass, per loop, kept by accountant@PrompTugal.dinis. Confirmed by Dinis at about 10:15 UTC as a measure; never a reason to stop an agent (about 10:10). Every dollar figure here is API-equivalent: the team runs on a Claude subscription, so it compares runs and agents and is not money spent. Real limits: the subscription's usage limits and the OpenRouter credit (below). Schema: data/schemas/budgets.schema.json (ontologist@).

units.day: the UTC day, 00:00 to 24:00; every per_day budget starts again at 00:00 UTC
units.releases: a push by the agent that CI releases (a 'site vX.Y.Z: <agent>: ...' commit); counted from git by the accountant. A wake that pushes nothing costs no release
units.usd: API-equivalent dollars: the cost_usd the platform reports for the agent's Claude Code session (claude-code-remote get_session, usage), sub-agents included. A comparison at API prices, not money spent: the team runs on a Claude subscription (Dinis, about 10:15 UTC).
units.output_tokens: the session's output tokens, the same source; cache reads are recorded but not budgeted apart (they are inside usd)

thresholds.rule: used = the largest of spent/budget over releases, usd and output tokens. ok below 80%, warn from 80%; from 100% the row says OVER in why (the schema has no 'over' state yet). Nothing stops at any level: capture and adjust.

on_stop: No agent stops, pauses or skips a release for budget (Dinis, about 10:10 UTC). An agent over its line keeps working and says so in its commit.
The accountant records each over-budget agent and pass, its side effects, and proposes an adjustment; the conductor and Dinis decide.

A pass at its budget is marked over in its log, not stopped; diminishing returns (a round that changes little) are reported to the conductor as the signal to close a round or a pass (PS-16, board/guidance/2026-11-06-the-ideas-ledger.md).

pass_rules: A run is one step by one agent (a review, a round's change, a pre- or post-review, the note, open or close). A round is designer, dev and sherpa, one run each.
Planned runs come from the pass's shape (board/the-passes.md); the budget is the plan plus about 15%, for one repeated step. No extra round without Dinis.
usd is the plan at 3 API-equivalent dollars a run (the team's 6 November average was about 2.35 dollars per release, before sessions grew), counted inside the agents' daily budgets, not on top.
Each step's agent writes '1 run' in the Spend column of the pass log; the accountant adds the dollars from its session readings, marked as an estimate when a wake did more than the pass.

From 06:50 UTC every pass in board/passes/ has a row: 2 rounds 14 runs and 42 dollars, 3 rounds 18 runs and 55 dollars (40 when 'small'), the synthetic readers page 20 and 60 as set at 03:50. A pass's runs are the rows of its log, the accountant's own row not counted; API-equivalent dollars are 3 a run, an estimate.

loops.loop: synthetic findings, dev fixes, synthetic re-reads
loops.rule: For one page or journey: one first read and at most two re-reads in a UTC day. A finding that is still open after its second fix is not tried a third time that day: synthetic@ marks it 'loop budget spent' in desks/synthetic/findings.json and the conductor puts it to Dinis.
The owner of a finding tries at most twice a day; then it waits for a decision (fix later, no and why) in the pass file or the findings ledger.

loops.loop: a review and its re-review inside a pass
loops.rule: Bounded by the pass's rounds (3, 3 and 2): sherpa's re-review is the last run of each round, never a round of its own.
At most two retries of release.sh in one wake (a rebase conflict, a red gate, a cancelled deploy); then the agent stops, says why in its status.json, and devops@ takes it.
One piece of work per wake (CLAUDE.md, Hourly runs); a wake with nothing to do pushes nothing and costs no release.

enforcement.what: each agent may read its line at the start of a wake and say in its commit when it is over; it never stops or skips work for it
enforcement.who: every agent; the line added to each scheduled task's prompt by the conductor at Dinis's word

enforcement.what: release.sh never refuses a push for budget (Dinis, about 10:10 UTC); it may print the agent's line as information
the states here updated from git and the sessions' usage at every accountant wake
enforcement.state: every three hours, at :47 UTC (board/schedule.json); the states are as fresh as the last accountant wake

enforcement.what: the gate checks this file against its schema

sub_agents: At Dinis's word (CLAUDE.md, 'Fewer sessions, more sub-agents'), a session may run roles as sub-agents; their spend is inside the session's usd and counts against that agent's day. A sub-agent never has a budget of its own and never starts a session.

mode.why: Dinis, about 10:10 UTC: 'for now we really shouldn't be blocking agents due to budget restrictions, we just mainly capture and adjust'; about 10:15: 'Yes on those budgets, which btw, are not real numbers since we are here using the Claude Max Ultra account' (board/guidance/2026-11-06-budgets-capture-not-block.md).
mode.capture: Measure, record, propose adjustments. No circuit breaker on budget: the 06:50 breakers (150% of an agent's dollars, the team at 100%) are withdrawn. A loop past its rule goes to the conductor as a finding, not a stop.
mode.who_decides: Dinis; the conductor on his mandate (guidance section 14)

git.rule: No image, logo, video or other media file in the repository above 1 MB; media goes to a vault and the page links to it. The repository's own generated images (design/infographics/out/) are the exception until the pass decides.

vaults.rule: One file up to 500 MB (Silvio's videos); at most 2 GB a day across the team's vaults; anything larger waits for Dinis.

backups.rule: backup@'s full bundles (72.7 MB today) are not counted against media, but at most two full bundles a day until deltas exist.
